newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends down on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends down on profit-taking.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended sharply down on Wednesday due to profit-taking after sharp rises in the past few days, traders said.
The most active February 1997 contract ended at 20,340 yuan ($2,450) per tonne, losing 220 yuan. It opened at 20,650 yuan, hitting an intra-day high of 20,700 and a low of 20,310.
December fell 220 to 19,900, January 300 to 20,140, March 270 to 20,400, April 300 to 20,400 and May 230 to 20,400.
Combined volume fell sharply to 78,250 tonnes from 176,860.
Copper opened higher but profit-taking pushed prices down steadily for most of the session.
Traders said copper faced a technical correction today after excessive rises over the past few days.

"Many investors took advantage of overnight LME gains to liquidate their long positions at high levels," one trader said. "They did not care if the price fell slightly because they had made large profits over the past few days," he added.
Traders said technical charts indicated copper had the potential to rise further in the next few days.
"Lower volume today suggested many investors had not lost confidence in the market trend," a second trader said.
Traders expect copper to move around the 20,500-yuan level in the next few day in the absence of major negative news.
Aluminium ended up in slow trading. December rose 80 to 13,480 yuan per tonne, January 50 to 13,550 and February 400 to 13,810.
Combined volume rose to 340 tonnes from 160.
